parsedContent.correctedAnswer: The liquidity position of this company is improving overtime. In the year 2008 the company’s ability to meet short-term financial obligations is questionable. The ratio is below the standard ratio (2:1). In the year 2009, the current ratio grew at 2.3:1 (above the standard ratio), thus the company becomes able to meet its short-term financial obligation when they fall due. In the year 2008 this company turned its stock into sales 4.64 times a year while in the year 2009, stock was turned into sales 4.775times. The company’s improvement in stock turnover is relatively insignificant. It can also be noted that this company trades relatively slow-moving items. The item is generally lasts more than two months in stock (365/4.64=78.66days, in the year 2008 and 365/4.775= 76.44days). The debt/ equity ratio of this company is increasing overtime. In the year 2015 the company’s assets were almost financed by the shareholders’ funds. Debt capital was less than 5% of the shareholders’ funds. In the year 2009 the company’s capital structure considerably changed by increasing the proportion of debt capital to 28.88% of the shareholders’ funds. The profitability level of this company is declining overtime (9.63% to 8.62%) the decline in the profit of this company is associated with increase in the risk arising from increased debt capital in the company’s capital structure. The dividend payout ratio is increasing overtime. Nevertheless, increase in this ratio cannot be explained as improvement since it is arising from the fact that dividends are constant while profit is declining.
